text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today, adding to a sharp three-day climb of $5.60 (4.1%) from November 9 to today. The move reflects an oil price rebound: US crude has recovered to $89.62 per barrel after dipping below $90 last week on hopes for Iran de-escalation, and the company benefits directly when oil prices strengthen. Over the past two weeks the stock is still down 6.65%, but that decline occurred earlier when geopolitical tensions seemed to be easing and Russia's crude output rebounded to 8.73 million barrels a day, both suggesting lower future prices for oil producers.

The recent three-day bounce appears tied to recognition that any near-term peace in Iran conflicts is uncertain—despite Trump's statements, analysts still see little chance of lasting resolution—leaving oil markets vulnerable to fresh supply disruptions rather than the surplus conditions that weighed on prices last week.
